claims.evidence: Witness photos show an industrial engine/power unit with exposed top/valve area and hoses/wiring, but no clearly readable brand/model nameplate or markings are visible; the report does not confirm it is a Caterpillar C9 or that it is complete.

risks.risk: Wrong engine model/variant (C9 not confirmed); pricing depends heavily on exact model and configuration.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine nameplate/serial plate (or stamped model number) showing 'C9' and serial number, plus any data plate with configuration.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unidentified industrial engine/power unit parts-only, with model unknown.

risks.risk: Not actually complete (missing major components like turbo, alternator, injectors, ECM, sensors, intake/exhaust, or crank/heads).
risks.proof: A full inventory photo list laid out (or video) showing all major assemblies included, and a checklist against what is missing.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/parts-only with unknown completeness.

risks.risk: Condition unknown (may be seized, low compression, leaking, or damaged internally).
risks.proof: Video of a start/run test (even if brief) and/or compression/leak-down results; also any fault codes readout if ECM is present.
risks.if_unproven: Price as non-running/untested engine parts with potential internal damage.

risks.risk: Major parts may be non-original or replaced (injectors/turbo/sensors/gaskets), affecting value and compatibility.
risks.proof: Close-ups of part numbers on injectors, turbo, alternator, sensors, and gasket surfaces; receipts/service records if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used/unknown-spec parts with compatibility risk.

risks.risk: Hidden damage not visible in top/valve area photos (cracks, scoring, bent rods, head warping).
risks.proof: Photos of cylinder bores, crankshaft journals, and head underside (or borescope video), plus inspection report.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst-case for internal wear/damage.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine nameplate/serial plate showing make/model (C9) and serial number.
Photos/video showing the full engine as a whole (not just the exposed top), including all major accessories and whether anything is missing.
Start/run video (or proof it can be cranked and runs) and any available fault-code readout from the ECM.
Compression/leak-down test results (or borescope video of cylinders) and photos of any visible damage areas (cracks/scoring).
Close-ups of part numbers for key components (injectors, turbo, alternator, sensors) to confirm configuration and originality.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is an industrial engine/power unit with exposed top components, but the seller’s specific claim (Caterpillar C9 and completeness) is not verifiable from the photos. A worst-case parts-only valuation is still possible without model proof, but it should be priced as unidentified/untested and potentially incomplete.
